usage: 결과 + noun: the result of something
natural collocation for results being announced/released
attaches to a verb to express consequence: 노력한 결과 = as a result of trying
discourse connector linking a cause sentence to its outcome
examples: 열심히 준비한 결과 좋은 점수를 받았어요.
As a result of preparing hard, I got a good score.
-(으)ㄴ 결과 turns the first clause into the cause of the second
검사 결과가 아직 안 나와서 기다리고 있어요.
The test results haven't come out yet, so I'm waiting.
결과가 나오다 = results are released
과정보다 결과가 더 중요하다고 생각하세요?
Do you think the result matters more than the process?
common contrast pairing 과정 vs 결과
nuance: 결과 is the end outcome of an action or event and pairs naturally with 나오다 (come out) or 나타나다 (appear). It often contrasts with 과정 (process). The pattern -(으)ㄴ 결과 is a frequent intermediate connective meaning 'as the result of having done X.'
mistakes: Don't say 결과를 나오다 — 결과 takes 이/가 with 나오다: 결과가 나오다.
결과 is the outcome, not the cause; use 원인 or 이유 for the reason.

usage: 원인 is the objective, often negative, cause of a problem or event
natural collocation for investigating what caused something
X이/가 원인이 되다 = X causes/leads to
common with 근본적(인) when discussing root causes
examples: 화재의 정확한 원인은 아직 밝혀지지 않았어요.
The exact cause of the fire hasn't been determined yet.
원인 is used for problems, accidents, and phenomena
스트레스가 여러 질병의 원인이 될 수 있어요.
Stress can become the cause of various illnesses.
X이/가 원인이 되다 pattern
문제의 원인을 먼저 찾는 것이 중요해요.
It's important to first find the cause of the problem.
원인을 찾다 collocation
nuance: 원인 refers to the objective cause of a result, usually a problem, accident, or phenomenon, and pairs with 결과 as cause-and-effect. It is more analytical and impersonal than 이유, which is the personal reason/justification someone gives. You investigate an 원인 but you explain an 이유.
mistakes: Don't use 원인 for personal reasons like 'the reason I'm late' — use 이유 there.
원인이 되다 (becomes a cause), not 원인을 되다.

usage: common on immigration forms and in formal contexts
describes having an intended aim behind an action
Verb-는 것이 목적이다 states a purpose
examples: 이번 모임의 목적이 뭐예요?
What's the purpose of this gathering?
asking for the aim of an event
이 프로그램의 목적은 외국인을 돕는 것이에요.
The purpose of this program is to help foreigners.
목적은 -는 것이다 pattern
뚜렷한 목적 없이 그냥 시작했어요.
I just started without a clear purpose.
목적 with 뚜렷하다 (clear) or 없이 (without)
nuance: 목적 is the conscious aim or intention behind an action and is more goal-oriented than 이유 (reason) or 원인 (cause). It is common in formal/written contexts such as immigration forms (방문 목적) and reports. To say what something is for, use N의 목적은 ~는 것이다.
mistakes: Don't confuse 목적 (purpose) with 목적지 (destination, a place).
Use 이루다/달성하다 with 목적, not 하다: 목적을 이루다, not 목적을 하다.

usage: 과정 follows a noun to name a developmental process
Verb-는 과정에서 = while/during the process of
also means a formal course of study
examples: 한국어를 배우는 과정에서 많은 실수를 했어요.
I made many mistakes in the course of learning Korean.
-는 과정에서 expresses 'while in the process of'
결과도 중요하지만 과정도 소중하다고 생각해요.
The result matters, but I think the process is precious too.
과정 vs 결과 contrast
이 절차는 여러 과정을 거쳐야 해요.
This procedure has to go through several stages.
과정을 거치다 collocation
nuance: 과정 covers both the 'process' of how something unfolds over time and a formal 'course' of study (교육 과정, 박사 과정). The very common pattern -는 과정에서 means 'in the course of doing,' highlighting events that happen along the way. It naturally contrasts with 결과 (the final outcome).
mistakes: Don't write 과장 (exaggeration / section chief) when you mean 과정 (process) — different word.
Use 거치다 with 과정 for 'go through stages,' not 가다.

usage: very common compound for one's social relationships
be related, have to do with
X와/과 관계가 있다 = is connected to X
examples: 동료들과의 관계가 정말 중요해요.
The relationship with my coworkers is really important.
N과의 관계 structure
그 일은 저와는 아무 관계가 없어요.
That matter has nothing to do with me.
관계가 없다 = unrelated, none of one's business
두 사건은 서로 깊은 관계가 있어요.
The two incidents are deeply related to each other.
관계가 있다 expressing connection
nuance: 관계 covers both personal relationships (인간관계, 친구 관계) and abstract relations/connections between facts or events. With 있다/없다 it often means 'to be related / have to do with,' so 관계없다 is a common way to say 'irrelevant' or 'none of my business.' Use 와/과 to mark the other party.
mistakes: Don't say 관계를 있다; it's 관계가 있다.
관심 (interest) and 관계 (relationship) look similar but mean different things — don't mix them up.

usage: X이/가 Y에게/에 영향을 주다 = X affects Y
X에게/에서 영향을 받다 = to be affected by X
more formal than 주다; common in writing
pairs with 좋은/나쁜/큰 to describe the effect
examples: 날씨가 기분에 큰 영향을 줘요.
The weather has a big effect on my mood.
N에 영향을 주다 pattern
저는 부모님께 많은 영향을 받았어요.
I was greatly influenced by my parents.
영향을 받다 = be influenced
이 정책은 사회 전체에 영향을 미쳐요.
This policy has an impact on society as a whole.
영향을 미치다 is the formal/written form
nuance: 영향 is the influence or impact one thing has on another and works in two directions: 영향을 주다/미치다 (to affect) and 영향을 받다 (to be affected). 미치다 is more formal and frequent in written or news Korean, while 주다 is everyday speech. Mark the affected target with 에 (things) or 에게/께 (people).
mistakes: Don't swap the direction: the affecter 주다/미치다, the affected 받다.
Use 에 or 에게 for the target, not 을/를: 환경에 영향을 주다 (not 환경을 영향을 주다).

usage: 상황 follows an adjective/noun describing the state of affairs
상황이 좋다/나쁘다/심각하다 describe how things stand
상황에 따라(서) 다르다 = it depends on the situation
examples: 지금 상황이 너무 복잡해서 설명하기 어려워요.
The situation is so complicated right now that it's hard to explain.
상황이 복잡하다 collocation
이런 상황에서는 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠어요.
In a situation like this, I don't know what I should do.
이런 상황에서(는) framing
답은 상황에 따라 달라질 수 있어요.
The answer can change depending on the situation.
상황에 따라 = depending on circumstances
nuance: 상황 describes the overall set of circumstances surrounding a moment or event, broader than a single 경우 (case/instance). The phrase 상황에 따라(서) 다르다 ('it depends on the situation') is extremely common and useful for hedging. 이런/그런 상황에서 frames advice or reactions to a set of conditions.
mistakes: Don't confuse 상황 (situation) with 상태 (state/condition of a thing or body).
Use 에 따라 for 'depending on the situation,' not 으로: 상황에 따라.

usage: common when talking about job or contract terms
조건 follows a noun naming the relevant terms
조건에 맞는 사람 = a person who fits the requirements
examples: 이 회사는 근무 조건이 정말 좋은 편이에요.
This company's working conditions are really quite good.
근무 조건 collocation
지원하려면 몇 가지 조건을 갖춰야 해요.
To apply, you have to meet a few requirements.
조건을 갖추다 = fulfill requirements
그 조건에 맞으면 누구나 신청할 수 있어요.
If you meet those conditions, anyone can apply.
조건에 맞다 = fit the conditions
nuance: 조건 means both the requirements that must be satisfied and the terms/conditions of an arrangement (jobs, contracts, deals). With 갖추다 or 만족하다 it means 'fulfill requirements,' and with 맞다 it means 'fit/match the conditions.' It is more concrete than 상황 — 조건 are the specific terms, not the overall circumstances.
mistakes: Don't use 조건 for an if-clause grammar point; 'if' is expressed with -(으)면, while 조건 is the noun 'condition.'
조건에 맞다 (fit the conditions), not 조건을 맞다.

usage: 기준이 높다/낮다/엄격하다 describe how strict a standard is
based on / using N as the standard
성적을 기준으로 = on the basis of grades
기준에 맞추다 = to align with the standard
기준 follows a noun naming what the standard is for
examples: 회사마다 채용 기준이 달라요.
The hiring criteria differ from company to company.
채용 기준 = hiring standards
나이를 기준으로 줄을 섰어요.
We lined up based on age.
N을 기준으로 = using N as the criterion
이 제품은 안전 기준을 모두 통과했어요.
This product passed all the safety standards.
안전 기준 collocation
nuance: 기준 is the standard or yardstick against which things are measured, judged, or sorted. The phrase N을/를 기준으로(하다) means 'taking N as the basis/reference point' and is very common for explaining how something is organized or decided. Unlike 조건 (a requirement to meet), 기준 is the measuring criterion itself.
mistakes: Don't drop 으로 in the set phrase: it's N을/를 기준으로, not N을 기준.
기준 (standard) is not 기분 (mood) — be careful with the vowel.

usage: to some degree, roughly how much
어느 정도 알아요 = I know to some extent
그 정도면 충분해요 = that much is enough
한 시간 정도 = about an hour
울 정도로 = to the point of crying
examples: 한국어를 어느 정도 할 수 있어요.
I can speak Korean to some degree.
어느 정도 = to some extent
여기서 공항까지 한 시간 정도 걸려요.
It takes about an hour from here to the airport.
N 정도 = approximately
말도 못 할 정도로 피곤했어요.
I was tired to the point that I couldn't even speak.
-(으)ㄹ 정도로 expresses degree/extent
nuance: 정도 expresses degree or extent and, after a number, means 'about/approximately,' similar to 쯤 but slightly more flexible. The set phrases 어느 정도 ('to some extent') and 그 정도 ('that much') are essential intermediate vocabulary. The grammar -(으)ㄹ 정도로 means 'to the extent/point that,' showing how strong something is.
mistakes: 정도 after a number means 'about,' so don't add 약 unnecessarily — 한 시간 정도 already means 'about an hour.'
Don't confuse 정도 (degree/extent) with 제도 (system/institution).

usage: natural way to say a change appears/arises
분위기에 변화를 주다 = add a change to the mood
pairs with 급격한/큰/작은 to describe scale
examples: 요즘 날씨 변화가 너무 심해요.
These days the weather changes are too severe.
변화가 심하다 = the change is severe
새 환경의 변화에 적응하는 데 시간이 걸렸어요.
It took time to adapt to the changes in the new environment.
변화에 적응하다 collocation
생활에 작은 변화를 주고 싶어요.
I want to make a small change in my life.
변화를 주다 = introduce a change
nuance: 변화 is the noun 'change,' used for changes in states, trends, weather, society, or life, and is more abstract than the verb 변하다 (to change). 변화를 주다 means 'to introduce/make a change' (often for variety), while 변화가 생기다 means a change 'occurs.' Mark what one adapts to with 에: 변화에 적응하다.
mistakes: Use the verb 변하다/바뀌다 to say 'something changes'; 변화 is the noun, so don't say 변화하다 to mean a simple everyday change (it sounds formal/scientific).
변화를 주다 (make a change), not 변화를 하다 in this 'add variety' sense.

usage: 의미 있는 일 = a meaningful thing
common way to say something has no point
in the sense that / meaning that
축하하는 의미에서 = in the sense of celebrating
결과에 의미를 두다 = to attach significance to the result
examples: 이 단어는 두 가지 의미가 있어요.
This word has two meanings.
의미가 있다 in the literal 'meaning' sense
감사하는 의미에서 작은 선물을 준비했어요.
I prepared a small gift to express my gratitude.
-는 의미에서 = in the sense/spirit of
혼자 여행한 것은 저에게 큰 의미가 있었어요.
Traveling alone had great significance for me.
의미가 있다 in the 'significance' sense
nuance: 의미 covers both the literal 'meaning' of a word and the deeper 'significance/value' of an experience, so 의미가 있다 can mean 'is meaningful' as well as 'has a meaning.' The pattern -는 의미에서 ('in the sense/spirit of doing') is a useful intermediate connector for explaining intentions behind an action. 뜻 is a near-synonym but leans toward literal word meaning.
mistakes: For asking 'what does this word mean?' both 의미 and 뜻 work, but in casual speech 뜻 is more common: 무슨 뜻이에요?
Don't say 의미를 있다 — it's 의미가 있다.

usage: 중요한 역할을 하다 = to play an important role
맡다 = to be in charge of a role/part
common when sharing tasks in a team
examples: 가족 안에서 각자의 역할이 있어요.
Within a family, each person has their own role.
역할이 있다 = to have a role
선생님은 학생들에게 중요한 역할을 해요.
Teachers play an important role for students.
역할을 하다 = to play a role
이번 프로젝트에서 제가 발표 역할을 맡았어요.
I took on the presentation role in this project.
역할을 맡다 = take on a role
nuance: 역할 is the role or part someone or something plays, used for people in groups, family members, or even the function of objects and factors. 역할을 하다 means 'to play/serve a role,' while 역할을 맡다 stresses being assigned or taking on the part. Note the pronunciation: 역할 sounds like [여칼].
mistakes: Don't write 역활 — the correct spelling is 역할.
Use 맡다 for taking on a role, not 잡다: 역할을 맡다, not 역할을 잡다.
